content.user_title: Migrate Firebase Extensions to Cloud Functions
content.value_statement: Firebase Extension migrations require careful trigger, configuration, lifecycle, and packaging changes. This skill guides conversion to local Cloud Functions or reusable npm packages.
actual_capabilities: Inventories parameters, APIs, roles, lifecycle events, resources, files, and test scripts from an extension.
Creates a local functions source layout or a reusable npm package migration plan.
Maps supported Firebase Functions V1 triggers to their V2 equivalents.
Preserves legacy handler logic through documented destructuring compatibility patterns.
Migrates runtime options and functions.config values to V2 options and parameterized configuration.
Maps extension lifecycle events, IAM roles, and required APIs to declarative SDK features.
limitations: It does not deploy functions or publish npm packages.
Compatibility shims depend on support in the installed Firebase Functions SDK.
Generated migrations still require type checking, tests, and runtime validation.
Package guidance assumes Node 22 or newer and firebase-functions 6 or newer.

use_cases.title: Move an installed extension into an application
use_cases.description: Convert extension resources and handlers into a local functions source tree for direct application ownership.

use_cases.title: Create a reusable functions package
use_cases.description: Prepare package metadata, exports, peer dependencies, documentation, and V2 function entry points for distribution.

use_cases.title: Modernize legacy extension triggers
use_cases.description: Map V1 triggers, runtime options, configuration, and lifecycle handlers to supported V2 APIs.

prompt_templates.title: Assess a Firebase Extension
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Firebase Extension and list its parameters, APIs, roles, lifecycle events, triggers, files, tests, and migration risks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with an inventory before changing code.

prompt_templates.title: Build a local functions migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this extension into a local functions source layout. Migrate supported triggers to V2 and document required configuration.
prompt_templates.scenario: Integrate extension behavior directly into an application.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a reusable npm package
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a publishable package from this extension. Include exports, peer dependencies, lifecycle mappings, V2 handlers, and user documentation. Do not publish it.
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a shareable package while retaining deployment control.

prompt_templates.title: Preserve complex legacy behavior
prompt_templates.prompt: Migrate this complex V1 extension to V2. Preserve handler logic with compatible destructuring, migrate secrets safely, and identify required tests.
prompt_templates.scenario: Modernize a migration with complex business logic and configuration.

output_examples.input: Assess a Firestore extension with configuration parameters and an installation task.
output_examples.output: The assessment identifies the Firestore trigger, parameter types, required IAM roles, installation lifecycle mapping, and tests needed before migration.

output_examples.input: Convert an extension into a local Cloud Functions codebase.
output_examples.output: The result organizes V2 handlers under the functions source directory, maps configuration, preserves tests, and provides deployment guidance without deploying.

output_examples.input: Prepare an npm package migration for several legacy triggers.
output_examples.output: The result defines package requirements, export behavior, trigger mappings, compatibility notes, configuration documentation, and validation steps without publishing.

best_practices: Inventory every extension resource before editing handlers or package metadata.
Bind secrets explicitly and initialize dependent clients during onInit or through lazy getters.
Run type checks and tests for every migrated provider and trigger.
anti_patterns: Do not call parameter value methods during top-level module loading.
Do not assume every V2 provider supports the same compatibility destructuring.
Do not deploy functions or publish packages without explicit user review.

faq.question: What migration targets does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports local Cloud Functions source integration and reusable npm package preparation.

faq.question: Does the skill deploy migrated functions?
faq.answer: No. It can provide deployment guidance, but deployment remains a separate user-controlled action.

faq.question: Does the skill publish npm packages?
faq.answer: No. The source instructions explicitly prohibit running npm publish.

faq.question: How are legacy V1 handlers preserved?
faq.answer: Supported event providers can use documented destructuring patterns that expose legacy-compatible event properties.

faq.question: How are secrets migrated?
faq.answer: Secret-like configuration values use secret parameters, explicit function bindings, and delayed initialization.

faq.question: What validation is still required?
faq.answer: Run TypeScript checks, automated tests, emulator tests, and deployment review for the migrated project.
